title: Scarlet and smoke
caption: The central region of Gum 15, imaged by ESO's Very Large Telescope

recognition.text: Ranked #96 on ESO’s published “Top 100 Images” list (an institutional selection, not an audience score).

story: A smoky black silhouette winds through a red-tinged field. It is one of the dust lanes at the center of Gum 15, a large, sparse cloud of partially ionized hydrogen known as an HII region.

The dark patches seem to hold few stars because dust hides the glowing gas behind them. The few stars that do show up there lie between us and Gum 15, creating the illusion of a clear view onto the more distant sky.

The cloud is shaped by strong winds from stars within and around it. It sits near several large groups of stars, including a star cluster whose brightest member, HD 74804, is thought to have ionized Gum 15's hydrogen, and it is this ionized hydrogen that gives the whole scene its red hue. In wider images the nebula looks like a reddish purple clump slashed by dark, winding dust lanes.

understand.summary: This visible-light image was made with the FORS2 instrument on the Very Large Telescope, using B, V and R filters plus a hydrogen filter. The caption says the red hue comes from ionized hydrogen, but the full filter-to-color mapping is not published.
understand.eye: Long exposures on a large telescope gather much more light than the eye, so the faint red glow looks far stronger here than it would by eye.

behind.exposure: Not published on the source page.
behind.technique: Not stated by the source (single frame, stack, mosaic or panorama unknown).

explore: This image came from the ESO Cosmic Gems program, which uses telescope time unsuitable for science to make images for education and outreach, with the data archived for astronomers. It used the FORS instrument on the Very Large Telescope. ESO had already released a wider view of Gum 15 in July 2014, and this region sits in its top left quarter.
alt: A smoky black lane of dust winding through a red-tinged field of glowing gas, with a few foreground stars.
